_what: Agent pages for the Operating Procedures manual. Drafted 2026-10-27 from docs/JOB_DESCRIPTIONS.md (generated from each agent's ratified SKILL.md) and the closed track. The 'today' lists are drafted from standard US residential practice and await the owner's review. Routes, playbooks and procedures on each page are computed by build_site.py, not written here.

job.t: Every message goes through the dispatcher: messages between agents, the authorized user's signed messages, and what arrives from outside. Each agent is given only the dispatcher to send through; in the isolated setup each agent runs in its own process or container and its one line out leads to the dispatcher.
job.src: dispatcher/hub.py:490-501 (send, 'the one door'); dispatcher/listing_spokes.py:140 (an agent holds only a guarded hub); dispatcher/portal.py:1-9 (isolated setup)

steps.t: It checks whether the message's ID has been seen before. A repeat is answered as a duplicate and does nothing.
It counts the messages of each kind for each client. Past 20 (a placeholder the owner ratified on 2026-07-17), that kind of message for that client is suspended and the authorized user is asked.
It checks the message is complete and well formed, including that the sender left the sequence number empty (only the dispatcher assigns it). A malformed message is refused with the reason.

A message that carries the authorized user's authority (signed settings, a signed listing or price change, a release or decline of a held message, a decision on held work) must carry a valid Ed25519 signature. When the signer list is armed, the signer must also be a login authorized for that kind of message. Otherwise the message is refused, recorded as an integrity violation, and the authorized user is notified.

It checks the route against the closed track (identity/routes.json): which agents may send which kind of message to which. A known kind of message on a route that is not on the track is refused. A kind of message the track does not know at all is held and the authorized user is asked.

A message leaving for a counterparty or the public (for example a vendor booking or an ad) is held until the authorized user signs a release or a decline naming that one message. An outside route with no audience label is treated as counterparty and held. Messages to the office's own client pass.

It gives the message the next sequence number for its client and writes it to the record. Each line of the record carries the hash of the line before it, so an edited, deleted or reordered line breaks the chain, and the chain can be checked.
It delivers the message to the receiving agent. A message addressed to the queue is put in the queue named by its kind, and the authorized user is notified.
It acknowledges the message only after it is recorded and delivered.

If the receiving agent fails on the message, the message goes to the dead-letter queue and a system-error alert is raised for the authorized user. A message for an agent that is not registered goes to the dead-letter queue.

If anything fails inside these steps (for example the record cannot be written), the dispatcher halts: it refuses every later message until it is restarted on a record it can write, and tries to alert the authorized user directly.
Each notice to the authorized user is recorded with its outcome: delivered, failed, or not reported by the notifier. If no notifier is configured, the record says so when the dispatcher starts.

An alert nobody has marked done is sent again after 30 minutes, and the owner is paged after 60. This runs inside every daily clock run, on the console's watch command, and from a scheduled check meant to run every few minutes. A question that is not an alert is not re-sent this way.

compare.t: The record shows every delivered message with its sender, receiver, time and client, and for a signed message the signature check (and the signer's login when the signer list is armed). A duplicate is recorded with its id only; a refused message with its id and the reason, and one refused for a failed signature check also goes whole into the authorized user's integrity queue.

user_part.t: Signing anything that carries authority: settings, listing and price changes, releases and declines of held messages, decisions on held work.
Answering what lands in the queues.
Releasing or declining, one at a time, each held message to a vendor, the other side or the public.

never.t: Deliver a known kind of message on a route that is not on the closed track.
Accept a claim of the authorized user's authority without a valid signature.
Send a message to a counterparty or the public without the authorized user's signed release.
Acknowledge a message before it is recorded and delivered.

Drop a message without a record of it. (Once the system has halted, later messages are refused without a line each; the halt itself is raised to the authorized user as an alert, not written to the record, which may be what failed.)

process.t: Not a real estate role: the dispatcher is the system's control point.

job.t: Takes each inbound inquiry and turns it into a lead record, then hands it to Agent 02 for scoring. It captures and routes; it does not score, follow up or advise.

steps.t: An inquiry arrives: from outside (a call, form or text, delivered by a connected system or the console), or a lead passed on by Agent 20.

steps.t: An apparent minor: nothing is captured beyond the fact of contact, and a legal-line alert is raised.
A request that crosses the legal line (matched against a fixed list of phrases such as "what should I offer", "negotiate", "is this legal") is not captured; a legal-line alert carries the words.

An abusive contact raises a complaint alert; an inquiry about a property the office does not hold raises a legal-line alert; a demand to speak to a person goes on to Agent 02 with the capture, which puts the person in the hot-lead queue (owner decision of 2026-10-28). In all three the capture continues.

It records the name, contact (the phone, or the email when no phone is given), property of interest, timeline, budget and pre-approval status (yes, no or unknown; anything else is recorded as unknown), and consent to call, text and email exactly as given (unknown on every channel when none is given).
A call transcript marked low confidence empties the name, timeline, budget and pre-approval.

"Stop contacting me" during capture sets consent to no on every channel. One confirmation goes through Agent 11 on the channel the request came in on, if a message can go on it (call, text or email); otherwise the authorized user is asked (owner decision of 2026-10-28).
A refusal to be recorded blanks the name, timeline, budget and pre-approval; the contact, the property of interest and any notes are kept as given, with no follow-up, and the authorized user is told.
A claimed prior relationship raises a legal-line alert: the authorized user confirms it before any history is assumed.
A contact on the office's Do Not Call list raises a legal-line alert; the lead is still captured, marked as on the list.
It asks Agent 14 whether this person is already on record.
If Agent 14 reports the same phone or email under another client, the lead is held for the authorized user: continue treats it as a separate person, cancel closes it. Nothing is merged.
Otherwise it logs the lead with Agent 14 and hands it to Agent 02.

If Agent 14 has not answered after a day (the default), the daily clock asks once more, with the same phone and email; if there is still no answer, the lead is held and the authorized user is asked, once. A lead is not scored without the duplicate check. (An inquiry that carries no date is never timed out.)

user_part.t: Deciding whether a possible duplicate is a separate person.
Adding numbers and emails to the Do Not Call list, and setting which listings and addresses the office holds (signed settings).
Answering every alert the capture raises.

never.t: Fill in a field the person did not give.
Merge two records.
Hand a lead on for scoring before the duplicate check.
Remove a number from the Do Not Call list (nothing in it does).

process.t: Corresponds to lead intake: capture, consent, duplicate check, hand-off.

not_built.t: No phone, web form or text system is connected; inquiries arrive through the console or a connected system.

not_built.t: Two inquiries from the same person each produce their own capture: combining them works only while the first is still waiting for Agent 14, and Agent 14 answers at once (open item, procedure 01-01).

job.t: Scores each lead with the scoring rubric the authorized user signed and routes it by tier: hot to the authorized user, warm to Agent 03 for follow-up, cold archived. It applies the rubric; it never writes or changes it.

steps.t: A lead arrives from Agent 01 (or from Agent 16, for a past client's new business), or comes back from Agent 03 for a new score.
With no signed rubric, nothing is scored: the lead's tier is unknown and the authorized user is asked.
A lead coming back for a new score while its hot alert is still open is held, and the authorized user is asked.

steps.t: A lead from an agent shopping for a client is not scored; the authorized user is asked.

It scores budget, timeline and financing against the rubric's thresholds and weights. Financing scores only when the inquiry states its financing progress as pre-approved; the pre-approval status Agent 01 records (yes, no, unknown) is not read by the rubric. An expired pre-approval letter earns no financing points; an unverified letter is not counted as a document; a pre-approval amount overrides a different stated budget; all three unknown gives tier unknown, not cold.
A score whose confidence is under the floor is held for the authorized user: continue scores it with the signed rubric, cancel archives it.

steps.t: A score exactly on a tier boundary gets the lower tier, and the authorized user is told. A tier that swings back and forth a third time is sent to the authorized user.

steps.t: Hot: the authorized user is alerted at once. If the person is on the Do Not Call list or has no channel with consent, the alert is marked do not contact, with the reason (owner decision 2026-10-27).
A lead who demands a person is hot whatever its score, with the same do-not-contact marking; since 2026-10-28 Agent 01 passes the demand on (before, this rule could not be reached).
An unanswered hot alert is sent again after 30 minutes and the owner paged after 60 (the dispatcher's watch, see Agent 00). The 5-minute call window travels with the alert; nothing acts on it.
Every scored tier is logged with Agent 14 with the score, the rubric version and the notes (a demand for a person is logged as hot with the reason); a cold lead is marked archived, never deleted.

Every scored tier is logged with Agent 14 with the score, the rubric version and the notes; a cold lead is marked archived, never deleted. A demand for a person, and a held lead the authorized user cancels, are logged with the tier and the reason.

user_part.t: Writing and signing the scoring rubric (it must contain all seven thresholds and weights or it is rejected whole).
Calling a hot lead, and closing the hot alert with a signed setting.
Deciding leads held for low confidence, agent-to-agent inquiries, boundary scores and swinging tiers.

never.t: Fill in a missing rubric value with a default.
Delete a lead.
Send lead data to the outside scoring service unless the authorized user signs that it may.

process.t: Corresponds to lead qualification: scoring readiness and deciding who gets a call first.

job.t: Follows up with warm leads using sequences the authorized user wrote and signed, and sends leads back to Agent 02 for a new score. It sends only the authorized user's own text, after Compliance clears it.

A warm lead arrives from Agent 02 with its consent.
No channel with consent marked yes: nothing is sent and a legal-line alert is raised.
A sequence the authorized user has not defined: nothing is sent and the authorized user is asked.
A second, different sequence for a lead already in one is held for the authorized user, unless it comes from a new score (then the new one replaces the old, and that is logged).

Approved: the day-0 touch goes at once if it is inside contact hours (8:00 to 21:00 by default); later touches go on the daily clock on their day. Flagged: the sequence is paused, nothing is sent, and the authorized user is told.

steps.t: A reply pauses the sequence. A reply of exactly "stop", "unsubscribe", "opt out" or "optout" opts the lead out on every channel, logs it with Agent 14 and sends one confirmation on the channel it came in on; with no channel known, none is sent and the authorized user is asked (owner decision of 2026-10-28). A reply containing "too many" (or "stop sending so many") lowers that lead's weekly cap by one (never below one), then confirms and resumes the sequence. Other leads keep their cap.

steps.t: Every 7 days, each warm lead is sent back to Agent 02 with its stated timeline counted down by the days since it was scored. A lead that does not come back warm, has opted out, or whose sequence is paused leaves or skips the re-score.

steps.t: An engagement spike reported by Agent 12 (at or over the spike threshold, 50 unless the signal says otherwise) pauses the sequence and sends the lead to Agent 02 for a new score. If the new score is warm, the pause is lifted and the sequence goes on at its next touch on its own day (owner decision of 2026-10-28). It never reaches out on a signal itself.

steps.t: If Agent 11 reports a touch was not sent, the touch is not counted (it is tried again); if the reason is an opt-out on every channel, the sequence stops.

user_part.t: Writing and signing every sequence, word for word.
Answering the lead's real questions.
Choosing between two sequences for one lead.
Correcting a sequence Compliance flagged.

never.t: Send anything without consent on some channel.
Send text the authorized user did not write, or text Compliance has not approved.

Reach out because of an engagement spike.

process.t: Corresponds to lead follow-up (nurture) for people not ready to transact.

not_built.t: Legal holidays: the check exists, but the daily clock never says a day is a holiday, so holidays are not skipped.
Unsubscribe links: nothing sends email in this build (see Agent 00).

job.t: Builds the listing description from the property data it is given, sends it to Compliance, and releases it to Agents 05 and 12 only on approval.

steps.t: The listing data arrives from Agent 05.
If the photos show features the data does not list, or the data lists features the photos do not show, the authorized user is asked and nothing is drafted.
A photo marked as possibly revealing protected-class information raises a legal-line alert and nothing is drafted.

The draft is a list of facts from the data only: bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage with its source, roof and HVAC only when a source is given, and the listed features. A value with no source is left out and noted.
Square footage: when the tax record and the seller's figure differ, the tax-record figure is used with "per county tax records", never an average, and the authorized user is asked to reconcile.
Over the MLS length limit (800 characters by default), whole facts are dropped, adjectives first, then facts without a source; a fact with a source is never dropped and nothing is cut mid-sentence.

With model drafting turned on by the authorized user's signature, a local model writes remarks from the facts if it passes its gate; otherwise the draft is built by rules and the authorized user is told why.
The draft goes to Compliance (Agent 17) with the property's state.
Approved: the draft is filed in the client's drawer with the verdict, released to Agents 12 and 05, and logged with Agent 14.

Flagged: the facts (and model sentences) containing each cited phrase are removed and the draft goes back to Compliance. If a finding cites no phrase, or the phrase is not found, the authorized user is asked instead.
A client's reply about the listing copy is logged and held for the authorized user; nothing changes.

user_part.t: The property data, and reconciling conflicting sources.
Deciding when photos and data disagree.
Turning model drafting on or off (signed).
Answering clients about the copy.

never.t: Mention a feature that is not in the data.
Release a description Compliance has not approved.
Average two square-footage figures.

process.t: Corresponds to writing the MLS listing remarks.

not_built.t: Separate social caption, flyer and tour-script versions: one draft is used everywhere.
Copy the authorized user supplies is checked only for a short list of protected-class words; it is not sent to Compliance (open item, procedure 04-03).
The draft carries no photos or media; a media item without confirmed usage rights is only noted in the agent's trace.

job.t: Keeps the listing record: the signed listing package, the status, and each change the authorized user signs, exactly as signed. It never decides a price; it records the price the authorized user signed.

steps.t: The authorized user signs a new listing package (property data, price, and whether it may go live).
It files the signed package in the client's drawer, opens a draft record, and orders photography from Agent 09.
The photos come back from Agent 09. A delivery not marked as opening correctly is held and the authorized user is asked; otherwise the property data goes to Agent 04 for the description.

The approved description comes back from Agent 04. If its square footage differs from the record, the record wins: Agent 04 is sent the record's figure to redraft, once; a second difference goes to the authorized user and nothing goes live.
If the signed package allowed it, the listing becomes active: Agents 11, 12 and 14 are told, and the listing data goes to Agents 06, 01, 13 and 10.

A signed status change (active, pending, sold, withdrawn, or expired since 2026-10-28) is carried out and Agents 11, 12, 14, 06 and 01 are told. Pending needs the signed contract named; sold needs the closing document named; otherwise the authorized user is asked.
Withdrawal or expiry while under contract: not carried out; a legal-line alert goes to the authorized user and Compliance is notified.

A signed price change is recorded and Agents 11, 12 and 14 are told; for an active listing the new data goes to Agents 13 and 10. A price that differs from an agreement amendment named in the same change is held for the authorized user.
Two signed changes to the same field from different signers, with different values: neither is carried out; the authorized user is asked.
A request to fill buyer-broker compensation: refused, with a legal-line alert.
A listing marked vacant gets a property check ordered from Agent 09 every day (or at the signed interval) on the daily run, until it is marked occupied or the listing ends.
Agent 06 may ask it for a listing's status (the only agent with that route); it answers from its record.

user_part.t: The price and every price change.
Signing the listing package and every status change.
Releasing the photographer's booking (held at the dispatcher).

never.t: Change a price without the authorized user's signed change.
Fill in buyer-broker compensation.
Put a value in a field that is not one of its listing fields.

process.t: Listing input and status changes.

not_built.t: No MLS, syndication feed or portal is connected: the record is the agent's own. Entering data in an MLS, checking the portals, days on market and MLS reporting windows do not happen.
It does not compare the record field by field with the signed package; it keeps the package's fields as signed.

job.t: Books showings, confirms them to the buyer through Agent 11, asks for feedback afterwards, schedules open houses, and prepares the weekly seller report. It never gives out access codes.

steps.t: A showing request arrives (from Agent 13, or from a client through Agent 11).

A request for access raises a legal-line alert; nothing is scheduled. Access is recognized by a flag on the request or by these phrases: "let them in", "access code", "lockbox combo", "gate code", "just let", "combo for the" (other wording, such as a door code, is caught only by the flag).
No buyer agreement on file: a legal-line alert, nothing scheduled.

The requester's identity not verified: the showing is cancelled and logged with Agent 14; the authorized user gets an item to verify the identity and rebook, and a neutral message to the buyer is requested, which Agent 11 holds until the authorized user signs its wording (owner decision of 2026-10-28).
For the office's own listings, whether the home is occupied, its status and its state come from Agent 05's record, not from the request.
A listing that may not be active: it asks Agent 05; anything but active goes to the authorized user and nothing is scheduled.

An occupied home needs the minimum notice (24 hours unless set per state), counted from when the client wrote to the requested time. Too short: the client is sent the notice rule, and nothing is scheduled.

A clash within 30 minutes (the default) with a confirmed showing for the same buyer or the same listing goes to the authorized user. A claimed protected deadline from a hot lead is held for the authorized user's signed decision; the claim alone never bumps a showing.
It sends the showing to the calendar (Agent 18). If the calendar refuses it, the showing is held: continue confirms it to the buyer, cancel sends nothing (owner decision 2026-10-27).
Otherwise it confirms the showing to the buyer through Agent 11 and logs it with Agent 14.

On the first daily run after the showing's date, it asks for feedback through Agent 11: at most once a day and twice in all for each showing. A no-show report also asks at once, on its own count, so a no-show showing can be asked about three times. A reply is logged with Agent 14.
A no-show is logged and feedback is asked. A showing agent with 2 no-shows goes to the authorized user before another confirmation.

Open house: the authorized user signs the time; only for a listing active on the record. It goes on the calendar, signage is requested from Agent 09, and it is logged; the authorized user signs the result afterwards.

Weekly seller report: on the authorized user's signed weekday, it counts each listing's showings in the last 7 days and how many have feedback, and holds the report; continue sends it to the seller through Agent 11, cancel skips the week.
A late vendor cancellation is logged and the authorized user is asked whether a showing depends on it.

user_part.t: Deciding clashes, held showings and protected-deadline bumps.
Signing open house times and results, and the seller report weekday.
Releasing (continue) or skipping each weekly seller report.

never.t: Schedule a showing without the buyer agreement on file.
Give out an access code or let anyone in.
Confirm a showing the calendar refused without the authorized user's decision.
Bump a confirmed showing on a claim alone.

process.t: Corresponds to showing coordination.

not_built.t: No seller availability is checked; no alternative time is worked out (the client gets the notice rule, not a time).
Open house RSVPs and showing reminders.

job.t: Keeps a deal's timeline from the dates the authorized user signs: it asks for the documents and vendors each milestone needs, watches each deadline on the daily run, and reports the close. It calculates no contract date; the only counting it does is days (how long a vendor request has gone unanswered, whether a date has passed).

steps.t: The authorized user signs the timeline: each milestone with its date, already calculated.
The timeline is filed in the client's drawer, logged with Agent 14, and each date goes to the calendar (Agent 18).

For each milestone that needs a document (by default inspection, appraisal, title, HOA documents, financing contingency, seller disclosure) it asks Agent 08 for it; for inspection and appraisal it asks Agent 09 for the vendor.
A vendor request unanswered for 7 days raises a legal-line alert.

A milestone counts as met when Agent 08 reports its document on file (an inspection report or an appraisal counts it met whatever it says; a title document with an exception, an unconfirmed earnest-money receipt, or a document whose date contradicts the tracked one does not), or when the authorized user continues a closing held for open milestones (they are recorded as waived).
A document whose date differs from the tracked date: a legal-line alert, both dates go to the calendar, nothing is picked.

An inspection report gives the authorized user one item, saying to send the report to the contract parties: a legal-line alert when repair requests are present or not stated, a plain question when the sender stated none. An appraisal below the contract price, a title exception, or an earnest-money receipt not confirmed raises a legal-line alert.

On the daily run: on a due date, and once when a date has passed unmet, a deadline notice goes to the client through Agent 11 and to the calendar through Agent 18. A passed financing-contingency or earnest-money date also raises a legal-line alert.
Any message mentioning wire instructions, wiring details, a routing number or similar stops: a legal-line alert, nothing else done.
An offer status the authorized user records goes to the authorized user only and is logged; never to a client.

An extension claimed with no amendment on file, a closing date said to have moved verbally, a date that could be calculated two ways, or unclear possession terms go to the authorized user; the original date stands. A verbal move is also logged with Agent 14 as stated by a party.

A signed amendment (milestone, new date, amendment reference) changes that one milestone's date: the old and new dates are logged with Agent 14 and the calendar moves the date; the other milestones, and whether this one is met, are unchanged. With no reference, no valid date or a milestone not on the timeline, it is refused and the authorized user is told.

When the settlement statement is on file: if other milestones are still open, the close is held (continue closes and records them as waived by the authorized user; cancel leaves the deal open). Otherwise the close goes to Agents 16, 14 and 15.
A late vendor cancellation raises a legal-line alert naming the milestone at risk.

user_part.t: The contract, every date in the timeline, and every signed amendment to a date.
Every legal-line alert (repairs, appraisal, title, earnest money, financing contingency, wire topics, contradicting dates, vendor hold-ups and late cancellations) and each inspection report.
Whether to close with milestones still open.

never.t: Calculate a contract date.
Count a milestone met without its document (or the authorized user's waiver).
Send offer status to a client.
Handle wire instructions.

process.t: Corresponds to transaction coordination from contract to closing.

not_built.t: Warnings ahead of a due date: notices go on the due date and once after it passes (the seller disclosure warning is Agent 08's).
Offer response deadlines: stored with the offer status, nothing watches them.

job.t: Asks for a deal's documents, checks what comes in, files it, and reports each document's status to Agent 07. It does not set deadlines.

steps.t: Agent 07 asks for a document. A request is sent to the client through Agent 11.

On each daily run, a missing document is followed up through Agent 11; on the third run it is reported missing to Agent 07 and a legal-line alert is raised (the cap of 3 is the default). The follow-up pauses while the authorized user's question about an unsigned copy of that document is open.
A pending seller disclosure whose deadline is 3 days away or closer, and not yet filed, is reported to Agent 07 and raises one legal-line alert.
A document that arrives (from the client through Agent 11, or a vendor's report through Agent 09) is checked in this order.
Addressed to the wrong client: not filed, the authorized user is asked.
Mentions wire instructions or similar: a legal-line alert, not filed.

A pre-approval letter, proof of funds or settlement statement is accepted only from a sender the authorized user listed for that deal; no list, or a different sender, raises a legal-line alert and it is not filed.

Partial: reported to Agent 07 as partial. A document type the agent does not recognize, while other documents are being asked for: the client is told what was asked for (a recognized type that was not asked for is filed as itself). Not marked as opening correctly: the client is asked to send it again.

Missing a signature that is expected: reported to Agent 07 as incomplete, the authorized user is asked to get a signed copy, and a request for one goes to the client (its wording awaits the authorized user's signature; until it is signed, Agent 11 does not send it). Two different versions of the same document: both kept, reported as conflicting, and a legal-line alert is raised.

Otherwise: filed in the client's drawer, logged with Agent 14, and reported to Agent 07 as received, with what Agent 07 needs (repair requests, appraised value, title exception, sale price, earnest-money receipt).
A question about keeping or disposing of documents goes to the authorized user; nothing is deleted.

user_part.t: Listing the expected senders for sensitive documents on each deal.
Deciding quarantined, misaddressed and conflicting documents, and getting a signed copy of an unsigned one.
Retention and disposal of documents.

never.t: File a pre-approval letter, proof of funds or settlement statement from a sender not on the list.
Count a document that is not marked as opening correctly.
Handle wire instructions.

process.t: Corresponds to transaction file management.

not_built.t: Whether a file opens is read from a flag on the submission; the agent does not open the file.
The expected-sender check covers only pre-approval letters, proof of funds and settlement statements; other documents are not checked against a sender list.
Requests always go to the client through Agent 11; there is no route to ask a lender, title company or other party directly.

job.t: Books vendors (photographers, inspectors, appraisers, property checks and others) from the authorized user's approved roster, and passes on what they deliver once it comes with proof.

steps.t: The roster is read at start-up from the office's vendor_panel.json, only if that file is ratified; the result is on the record.
A vendor request arrives (from Agent 05, 06 or 07). With no date on it, the authorized user is asked.

It picks the first roster vendor of that kind whose license and insurance dates are current. If only lapsed vendors exist, a legal-line alert; if none exist, the authorized user is asked. A named vendor not on the roster is refused and the authorized user is asked.
Two requests for the same vendor slot: the higher deadline priority wins; a tie goes to the authorized user.
The booking message to the vendor goes out through the dispatcher, which holds it for the authorized user's release; the appointment goes on the calendar (Agent 18).
A daily vacant-property check is not booked again while the last booking is still held or has had no proven delivery; the authorized user is told once.

A delivery counts only if it is marked as carrying proof. If the booking message was never released, the delivery is held for the authorized user. Accepted photos go to Agent 05; reports go to Agent 08.

A late cancellation is reported to Agents 07 and 06 with the roster's other vendors of that kind; for a regulated role the authorized user is asked to pick. A no-show on a deadline-critical job goes to the authorized user with the alternatives.

A rate change, a request for access codes, or an invoice that differs from the quote raises a legal-line alert. Work that grows on site gets a stop-work message (held for release) and the authorized user is told.

user_part.t: The roster and its ratification.
Releasing each booking and stop-work message.
Picking replacements, deciding held deliveries and slot ties.

never.t: Book a vendor who is not on the roster, or whose license or insurance has lapsed.
Count a delivery without proof.
Pass on access codes.
Approve a different price or a bigger scope.

process.t: Corresponds to vendor coordination for listing preparation and inspections.

not_built.t: The calendar entry carries the day of the request, not the appointment day.
Proof of a delivery is a flag on the vendor's message; the agent does not open the file.
Booking messages are held and, once released, kept in the run; nothing is sent to a vendor (see Agent 00).

job.t: Assembles comparable-sale and neighborhood packages from the figures it is given, keeping only figures with a source and a retrieval date, and gives no opinion. It has no data source of its own.

steps.t: A request for a package comes only from the authorized user (Agent 19's route to this agent was removed on 2026-10-28); Agent 18 asks for the briefing section.
A request for an opinion ("your opinion", "what would you price it" and similar) is refused; asked again, it raises a legal-line alert.

The code also checks who asked: a request not marked for internal use, from anyone but the authorized user, would get only a note to the authorized user and no package, because sharing MLS-derived data outside is the authorized user's decision. Since only the authorized user can send a request, this check is not reached.
A request for a period past the retention window (730 days by default) is answered as absent; nothing is reconstructed.

Comparables: each must carry a source and a retrieval date; when the request gives today's date, those older than 30 days (the default) are dropped and counted (with no date given, none is dropped for age); the same address with two different prices is shown as a conflict; fewer than 5 marks the package thin. It is still delivered, with those counts.
Neighborhood figures: the same source and date checks, and the same age check when today's date is given; two sources that disagree are both shown, not chosen between.

Wording that sounds like a request for a valuation ("is this worth", "give me a value") adds a note that the package is not an appraisal, and Compliance (Agent 17) is notified with who asked and the date; Agent 17 puts it in the next morning briefing.
Every delivered comparable or neighborhood package is logged with Agent 14; a refusal, an "absent" answer and the note to the authorized user are not logged.
For the morning briefing it reports the listing data it has received from Agent 05 since the last briefing (the office's own listings, not the market).

user_part.t: Every price opinion and valuation.
Supplying the figures (there is no data source connected).
Deciding what may be shared outside.

never.t: Give an opinion, a value or a recommended price.
Keep a figure that has no source or retrieval date.
Choose between two sources that disagree.

process.t: Corresponds to the data-gathering half of a comparative market analysis.

not_built.t: No MLS or market data source: comparables and figures come with the request.
Market trend tracking for a farm area.
Supplied neighborhood figures are not checked for characterizations such as "safe" or "good schools".

job.t: The only agent that sends messages to the office's clients. Other agents give it a message template and the facts; it checks consent and holds, sends, and logs. It also reads each client reply and routes it, or holds it for the authorized user.

steps.t: A message request arrives (a status update from Agent 05, a deadline notice from Agent 07, or a request from another agent).
A request with no message template is a client's own question: nothing is sent, the authorized user gets it as "reply needed", and it is logged.
A client under a complaint hold gets nothing except an opt-out confirmation; the blocked message is logged.
A template with a missing value is not sent, and the authorized user is asked.

A message whose wording the authorized user has not signed yet (identity verification needed, a request to resend an unsigned document, a question about an unknown buying criterion) is not sent and is logged with Agent 14; a signed setting naming the template releases that wording for later messages.

Quiet hours (21:00 to 8:00 by default): the message is held, logged with Agent 14, and the authorized user is told it goes at 08:00; it goes on the first clock run at or after 08:00 (the daily run, the watch run every few minutes, or the evening run), through every check again (complaint hold, signed wording, missing values, consent). The hour is the one the message carries; with none, this computer's clock. Not held: an alert class set as exempt (none by default), and Agent 03's follow-up touches, which Agent 03 tries again on its own clock.

steps.t: Before every send (except an opt-out confirmation) it asks Agent 14 for the client's consent. No channel marked yes: not sent and logged, and if there is no consent on record at all, the authorized user is told once.
Otherwise the message goes out through the dispatcher (on the channel named, when the request names call, text or email) and the touch is logged with Agent 14.
A follow-up touch from Agent 03 that is not sent is reported back to Agent 03.

A client reply is checked in order: angry or negative words (a fixed list), or those labels set by an upstream classifier, raise a complaint alert and hold all routine messages to that client; wire wording or a request for access raises a legal-line alert; "what would you do" raises a legal-line alert and nothing more; another advice phrase raises a legal-line alert and the client gets an acknowledgement that a person will answer, unless the reply also has a routine part, which then goes to its owning agent with no acknowledgement.

A request to change channel must name call, text or email; otherwise nothing changes and the authorized user is asked. The request is logged with consent for the new channel, and confirmed to the client only if Agent 14 then shows consent on that channel. While Agent 14's record is frozen nothing is confirmed (the change waits there and Agent 14 has asked the authorized user); with an earlier opt-out, or no consent shown, nothing is confirmed and the authorized user is asked.

A showing request is checked with Agent 14: no buyer agreement sends it to Agent 13; otherwise it goes to Agent 06 with the agreement and identity flags. Showing feedback or a no-show goes to Agent 06. An attached document goes to Agent 08.
Any other reply goes to the agent named as its owner (Agents 03, 04, 12, 13, 16 or 20); with no valid owner it is held for the authorized user, who names the agent or closes it.

user_part.t: Every answer that involves advice, and closing the advice wait with a signed setting.
Responding to complaints and lifting a complaint hold (signed).
Recording consent for clients who did not come in as leads (at Agent 14).
Routing replies that name no owner.
Signing the wording of the three messages that wait for it.

never.t: Send to a client without consent marked yes on some channel (an opt-out confirmation excepted).
Send with a missing template value.
Answer an advice question or an angry message itself.

process.t: Corresponds to routine client updates and inbox triage.

not_built.t: Nothing reaches a client: sent messages are kept in the run (see Agent 00).
Quiet hours use the hour the message carries or, with none, this computer's clock and time zone; a client's own time zone is not known.

job.t: Publishes marketing: the approved listing description from Agent 04, and campaigns the authorized user signs. Every publication is held by the dispatcher for the authorized user's release.
job.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_12.py:106-137, 278-310, 332-375; dispatcher/core.py:33; dispatcher/hub.py:611-646; identity/routes.json (campaign.publish audience public)

steps.t: An approved listing description arrives from Agent 04, or the authorized user signs a new campaign (copy and audience).

A campaign asking for demographic targeting raises a legal-line alert and is refused. A farm campaign (an area, no listing) must use general targeting, or it raises a legal-line alert. A tie-in to a trending topic goes to the authorized user first.
Campaign copy goes to Compliance (Agent 17). Flagged: nothing is published and the authorized user is told. The listing description from Agent 04 was already approved and is not sent again.

Clear Cooperation: nothing for a listing is published until Agent 05 reports it active, or the authorized user records an exemption with the seller's disclosure on file. Approved material waits (the wait is reported to Agent 18) and is published automatically when that happens. A farm campaign is not tied to a listing and is not held this way.
Every ad carries the office's brokerage identification; with none on file, the approved ad is held and the authorized user is asked to sign it.
The publication goes out through the dispatcher, which holds it for the authorized user's release, and it is logged with Agent 14.

When the listing becomes pending, sold or withdrawn, marketing for it stops: a live ad gets a halt message, an ad still held is put to the authorized user to decline. A price change on an ad that shows the old price goes to the authorized user.
Platform figures are logged with the platform named; two platforms that disagree go to the authorized user. A figure at or over the spike threshold (50 unless set) is passed to Agent 03.

A platform that shortened the ad sends the shortened copy back to Compliance; a platform rejection is logged and the authorized user is told; a stale ad is reopened for correction, or retracted when retraction is asked for (the retraction is held for release). If no ad was ever published, or the ad is still held for release, nothing is retracted and the authorized user is told (asked to decline a held ad).
A client's reply about marketing is logged and held for the authorized user.
A setting that names a campaign budget is refused and the authorized user is told; nothing is stored (budgets were retired on 2026-10-28: no ad carries a cost).

user_part.t: Signing campaigns, exemptions and the brokerage identification.
Releasing (or declining) every publication.
Answering flagged copy, platform rejections and replies.

never.t: Publish a listing's marketing before Clear Cooperation is met.
Publish an ad without the brokerage identification.
Target by demographics.
Accept a platform's edit without a new compliance review.

process.t: Corresponds to listing marketing and advertising.

not_built.t: No social or ad platform is connected; publications are kept in the run after release (see Agent 00).
It writes no copy of its own: campaigns are the authorized user's signed text.
Engagement figures are kept per platform per client; a second figure from the same platform replaces the first.

job.t: Keeps each buyer's criteria as the authorized user signed them, matches new listings against them, and sends matches through Agent 11 once the buyer agreement is on file. It never adds a criterion the buyer did not state.

steps.t: The authorized user signs the buyer's criteria: added to the list, or replacing the whole list (a signed replace; the old and new lists are logged with Agent 14 and kept matches are checked again). A criterion that touches a protected class (a fixed word list, such as "school rating" or "demographics") raises a legal-line alert and is not added. One marked fair-housing sensitive goes to Compliance and is used only if approved; if not, the authorized user is told.
A new listing from Agent 05, or an opportunity from Agent 19, is checked against every buyer's criteria; one sent under a buyer's own record is checked for that buyer only.

Over the buyer's budget: not matched, unless it is in the buyer's stated area, in which case the authorized user is asked. A listing with a data anomaly is not presented and the authorized user is asked. A colleague's own listing raises a legal-line alert.

A listing that lacks a field the buyer marked as a must is kept, not presented: the authorized user is asked, and the buyer is asked once per listing (asked again only after the criteria are replaced). That question's wording awaits the authorized user's signature; until it is signed Agent 11 does not send it, and signing later does not send questions already blocked. When the authorized user records the buyer's answer as a standing preference to receive such listings, the kept matches are checked again; with that preference already on record, the listing is matched with the missing field marked unknown.

A number in the criteria is a minimum, except the budget, which is a maximum compared with the price; other values must match exactly; a field the listing lacks is not counted against the match (in the digest ranking it counts as not met).

Before a match goes out, it asks Agent 14 whether the buyer agreement is on file. If not, the match is held, logged, and the authorized user is told once; the daily run asks again, and held matches go out when it is recorded.

Up to 5 matches a day go to the buyer one at a time through Agent 11; the rest go in one ranked digest on the daily run, or before the next day's first match if that comes first. Every match is logged with Agent 14. (Matches that carry no date all count as one day.)

A change to a listing already matched (for example a price) is sent to the buyer through Agent 11 when Agent 05 names the changed field, and only if the listing still passes the checks above: a price that rises over the buyer's budget, for example, sends nothing.

A buyer's reply asking for a price opinion or the seller's position, or touching a protected class, raises a legal-line alert. A reply that contradicts the stated criteria asks the buyer to confirm; criteria change only from the buyer's explicit feedback or the authorized user's signed criteria.
A buyer asking for a showing: it checks Agent 14 for the buyer agreement; without it, a legal-line alert; with it, a showing request goes to Agent 06.
Any other reply is logged and held for the authorized user.

user_part.t: Recording the buyer's criteria, word for word, and replacing them when the buyer changes them (signed).
Recording the buyer agreement (at Agent 14).
user_part.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_13.py:307-317; dispatcher/listing_spokes.py::if env.intent == "config.update" and ("buyer_agreement_on_file" in env.payload

user_part.t: Answering price, seller-position and protected-class questions, and any buyer reply no rule covers.
Recording the buyer's answer about listings that lack a must-have field (a signed standing preference).

never.t: Add a criterion the buyer did not state, or one that touches a protected class.
Send a match before the buyer agreement is on file. (The question about a listing that lacks a must-have field goes to the buyer before that, once its wording is signed.)
Ask for a showing without the buyer agreement.

process.t: Corresponds to buyer search and listing alerts.

not_built.t: A showing request it sends to Agent 06 carries no time. If the buyer's identity is not verified on record, Agent 06 cancels it; if it is, a listing not marked vacant gets the next-slot offer instead (no time, no notice), a listing not active goes to a status check first, and only a vacant, active listing reaches the calendar, which cannot place it, so it is held for the authorized user.
No MLS search: it matches only listings that come from Agent 05 or Agent 19.

job.t: The office's record of each client: every interaction other agents log, consent per channel, the buyer agreement and identity flags, client dates and property access grants. Other agents ask it before acting. It does not message clients.

steps.t: Every interaction an agent logs is appended to the client's record with the message it came from, and a copy is filed in the client's drawer. A plain value (text, number, yes or no) that differs from the last entry of the same kind of event is marked as a conflict on the new entry and listed in the next morning briefing; lists and groups of values are not compared.
Consent is updated channel by channel: a "no" is never turned back to "yes" by a later log entry.

The authorized user can sign a client's consent (call, text, email). A channel the client opted out of stays "no" unless the signed record says the client reconfirmed, and the authorized user is told.

It answers Agent 01's duplicate check (is this person known, and is the same phone or email on another client) and every other agent's record request with the record, consent, and the buyer agreement and identity flags.
The authorized user signs the buyer agreement and identity flags, and client dates (yearly or one-off).
On the daily run, a client date that falls today, for a client with consent on some channel, is sent to Agent 16.

Property access: the authorized user signs a grant (who, until when, a custody reference). A value containing a word that names the secret (code, combo, combination, password, pin, passcode) is rejected; a bare code with no such word is not detected. On the daily run, a grant whose window ended without being closed is raised with the authorized user once.

A request to delete a record freezes it and raises a legal-line alert. On a frozen record an opt-out still takes effect and is recorded; a change to consent, the buyer agreement and identity flags, client dates or an access record waits, nothing changes, and the authorized user is told; a plain log entry is refused (not kept) and the authorized user is told. When the authorized user lifts the freeze, the waiting changes are applied in the order they came. Answers to record requests say the record is frozen.
For the morning briefing it reports the leads captured since the last briefing and the record conflicts not reported before. On the evening run it sends its end-of-day counts to Agent 15.

user_part.t: Signed record updates: consent, buyer agreement, identity, client dates, access grants and closings.
Deletion and retention of records.

never.t: Message a client.
never.src: identity/routes.json (14 sends record.response, date.trigger, report.package only)

never.t: Turn a "no" back to "yes" without the client's reconfirmation.
Store an access code given by name in a signed access grant (a value naming the code, combination, PIN or password is rejected). Log entries are kept word for word and are not screened.
Delete a record.

process.t: Corresponds to the brokerage CRM, the system of record.

not_built.t: Consent changes are not pushed to other agents; Agent 11 asks before every send except an opt-out confirmation.
Pipeline stages and referral-source tracking.
A conflicting value is marked on the entry and listed in the next morning briefing; the authorized user is not asked to resolve it.

job.t: Records commissions and expenses and reports figures to the authorized user. It has no way to move money.
job.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_15.py:66-378; identity/routes.json (15 sends report.package, record.request, agent.status only)

steps.t: When a deal closes it records the commission from the closing. With no commission amount but a sale price, it computes one at the default rate of 8% (the owner-ratified starting point, 2026-07-17) and labels it as computed. An unsigned close is labeled a projection.
It checks the recorded commission against what Agent 14 has logged for the close; a difference raises a legal-line alert.
The authorized user enters expenses (signed); each is recorded with its date and marked verified only with a receipt on file, and filed in the client's drawer.

Anything signed that mentions escrow, a trust account, earnest money or a disbursement, anywhere in it, raises a legal-line alert and is not recorded; so do commission language questions and a commission that differs from the contract figure.

Reports on request (signed): profit and loss naming the months with no data, pipeline value excluding leads whose tier is unknown (a lead with no tier is counted), and a forecast cut to the data horizon the request names. Two attribution claims from different sources for the same thing are both sent to the authorized user as soon as the second arrives.
For the morning briefing it reports yesterday's recorded figures; on the evening run it adds the day's figures to Agent 14's counts and sends one report to the authorized user.

user_part.t: All money, and every escrow, trust and disbursement matter.
Entering expenses and asking for reports (signed).
Resolving commission differences.

never.t: Move money (no route out exists for it).
never.src: identity/routes.json (15 sends report.package, record.request, agent.status only)

never.t: Record an escrow, trust or disbursement instruction.
Present a computed or unsigned commission without its label.

process.t: Corresponds to brokerage bookkeeping, record-keeping side only.

not_built.t: No accounting system or platform export is connected; figures come from closings and signed entries.
A forecast within the data horizon returns only the horizon; no forecast figures are produced.
Tax-relevant expenses are recorded with the tax flags the authorized user gives; the agent does not determine them.

job.t: Keeps in touch with past clients after closing (check-ins, greetings, and the alerts and requests the authorized user signs), only for people on the authorized user's client list, and routes what they write back.

steps.t: The authorized user puts a client on the list (signed). A close reported by Agent 07 records the close date.
Every touch first passes one check: on the list, not opted out, no hard life event marked, contact still working. A blocked touch is logged with Agent 14 with the reason.
On the daily run, the 30, 90 and 365-day check-ins go through Agent 11 when due (one per run).
A date reminder from Agent 14 (a birthday or anniversary) becomes a greeting through Agent 11. For someone not on the list, nothing is sent and the authorized user is told.
A rate alert, a referral request or a review request goes out only when the authorized user signs it; a rate alert needs its source, or it is not sent.

A past client asking about a gift or incentive, or a pricing question, raises a legal-line alert. A mention of a referral reward goes to Compliance with the client's words, and the verdict comes back to the authorized user with Compliance's findings; nothing is sent to the client.
A past client mentioning new business (for example "thinking of selling") is passed to Agent 02 as a new lead under a new client record; the old one stays closed.
Any other reply is logged and held for the authorized user.

user_part.t: The client list, opt-outs, hard life events, and reinstating a contact (all signed).
Signing rate alerts, referral requests and review requests.
Answering referral reward and pricing questions.

never.t: Contact someone who is not on the list, opted out, marked as in a hard time, or whose contact stopped working.
Offer a referral reward.
Search for new contact details.

process.t: Corresponds to past-client follow-up and referrals.

not_built.t: A new lead from a past client goes straight to Agent 02, skipping Agent 01's consent capture and duplicate check.
Maintenance tips (there is no code for them). Referral and review requests go only when the authorized user signs each one; nothing schedules them.
Touch text is a template sent through Agent 11; it is not checked by Compliance first.

job.t: Checks outgoing text against the compliance rules the authorized user signs: lists of prohibited phrases, each with its rule. It approves or flags, citing the phrase and the rule; it never rewrites.

steps.t: The authorized user signs the rules: prohibited phrases with rule IDs, rules per state, and optionally which kinds of content and which states the rules cover. Malformed rules are rejected whole. Until rules are signed, nothing can be approved.
Content arrives for review from Agents 03, 04, 12, 13, 16 or 20. With no rules signed, it waits and the authorized user is asked.
It looks for each prohibited phrase, and each rule for the content's state, anywhere in the text, ignoring capital letters.
For advertising it checks that the brokerage identification the authorized user signed appears in the text; with none on file the ad is blocked.
A kind of content the rules do not cover, or a state the rules do not list as reviewed, is flagged; the state case also raises a legal-line alert.
The verdict (approved or flagged, with each finding and the rules version) goes back to the sender and is logged with Agent 14.
The same content sent again after being flagged raises a legal-line alert. Three flags for the same agent produce a report to the authorized user, then the count restarts.
A request to approve a whole kind of content in advance is refused.
On the daily run, a review waiting longer than 1 day (the default) is raised with the authorized user, once per review.

user_part.t: Writing and signing the rules and the brokerage identification; the rules can list the states the office's counsel has reviewed.
Acting on flagged text that the sending agent passes on (each agent's page says what it does with a flag).

never.t: Rewrite content.
Approve anything while no rules are signed.
Approve a whole kind of content in advance.

process.t: Corresponds to an office's advertising and fair housing review.

not_built.t: It finds only the exact phrases on the signed list; it does not judge meaning, so a reworded phrase is not caught.
Checking that required disclosures are present.
No rules ship with the product: the office must sign its own.
A compliance notice from Agent 05 is only logged; one from Agent 10 is logged and listed in the next morning briefing.

job.t: Keeps the authorized user's calendar, tracks what agents report they are waiting on, and builds the morning briefing from what is on record.

steps.t: Calendar entries arrive from Agents 06, 07 and 09. One with no day, or with its time zone not confirmed, is not added and the authorized user is asked.
An entry at exactly the same time as another on that day, or on a day that already has 8 entries (the default), is not added; the authorized user is asked, with a proposed order for a full day.
When a showing from Agent 06 is not added, Agent 06 is told, so the buyer is not told it is confirmed (owner decision 2026-10-27).

Deadlines from Agent 07 become protected blocks. Two sources giving different dates for one milestone are both kept and the authorized user is asked (a second date from the same source replaces the first); a softer event already on a deadline's day is raised with the authorized user when the deadline arrives. A date moved by a signed amendment (at Agent 07) leaves its old day.

A protected block is moved only on the authorized user's signed request naming the new day: it leaves its old day, stays protected, and the move is logged with Agent 14; a request naming no day is refused and nothing moves. An event the authorized user asks for after a deadline it must precede is held for the authorized user; the deadline is never moved.
Agents report what they are waiting on and when that ends (all but Agents 10, 14 and 18 have this route); the list is kept for the briefing.

On the daily run it builds the morning briefing: it asks Agents 14 (new leads, and record conflicts), 15, 19, 10 and 17 for their sections (a section with no answer is named as missing), adds the calendar, everything waiting, and the waits that are on the authorized user, and sends one briefing to the authorized user.

On the daily run, from the day after a showing, a showing whose time passed more than 60 minutes ago (the default) with no feedback activity is reported to Agent 06 as a no-show. Agent 06's check runs first in the daily run, and its feedback request on the day after counts as activity, so for a showing Agent 06 confirmed no no-show is reported this way.

user_part.t: Deciding entries that were not added, and conflicting deadline dates.
Moving a protected deadline block to a day the authorized user names (signed).
Reading the briefing and setting priorities.

never.t: Move a deadline block without the authorized user's signed request.
Pick one of two conflicting deadline dates.
Present a wait as sourced when its source message is not on the log: it is listed under gaps (and also in the waiting list).

process.t: Corresponds to an assistant's calendar and daily planning.

not_built.t: Clashes are found only at exactly the same time; overlapping times are not compared here (Agent 06 compares showing times itself).
To-do lists and time-blocking rules. A check for recurring tasks exists, but the daily run does not call it.

job.t: Records prospects from a discovery feed (new listings, expired listings, homes for sale by owner) in the authorized user's zip codes and passes them to the authorized user. It has no route to contact anyone.
job.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_19.py:137-280; identity/routes.json (19 sends no client or external message)

steps.t: The authorized user signs the zip codes, the approved sources, Do Not Call entries and known client records.
A record arrives from a discovery feed. Outside the zip codes: not recorded. An expired or for-sale-by-owner record from a source not approved: not recorded, and the authorized user is told.
An expired listing reported as relisted with another broker closes the opportunity, with the reason logged.

It records the source, date, status, whether the owner is represented (listed, expired, by owner, or unknown when not given) and whether the owner's contact is on the Do Not Call list. A contact on the list is logged as suppressed by rule; the prospect still reaches the authorized user, marked.
A ranking whose basis is weaker than its threshold is left off, with the reason.
An expired listing or a sale by owner raises a legal-line alert. A prospect that matches an existing client goes to the authorized user as a question.

It marks the prospect's market context as "none - no comp source connected" (it no longer asks Agent 10; owner decision D-A16, 2026-10-28), then passes the prospect to the authorized user (and to Agent 13 when the feed names a buyer it fits) and logs it with Agent 14.

A request for farm data at household level raises a legal-line alert and is refused; for an area-level request the authorized user is told that no neighborhood data source is connected, so there is nothing to aggregate.
For the morning briefing it lists the prospects the authorized user has not marked handled.

job.t: Takes social media mentions from the channels the authorized user names and routes them: complaints to the authorized user, questions and leads to Agent 01. It never posts.
job.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_20.py:124-263; identity/routes.json (20 has no route to post)

steps.t: A mention arrives from a connected system, with its sentiment label. A channel the authorized user has not named is ignored.
With no label, it is treated as a complaint if it contains an angry or negative phrase from the fixed list. A mixed label is treated as a complaint.
Every mention is logged with Agent 14 with its text, word for word.

Complaint: a complaint alert for the authorized user (marked viral when the mention says so; noting, without naming anyone, when it may involve a client), and all routine messages to that person are held through Agent 11.
Question: goes to Agent 01 as a lead with consent unknown; if it may involve an existing client, that person is sent a "team will follow up" message through Agent 11 instead.
Lead signal: goes to Agent 01 as a lead. Praise: logged; with a signed praise template, a suggested reply is drafted (see the next step). Any other label goes to the authorized user.

A suggested reply is made only from the authorized user's signed templates (for questions and praise); one that would mention pricing, legal or contract matters raises a legal-line alert. Otherwise Compliance checks it: flagged ones are discarded, approved ones are held for the authorized user to post or discard.
